title: Rectangular detection of a continuous homogeneous cocycle
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a topology for which addition, negation and multiplication $K\times K\to K$ are continuous, and let $G$ be a group with a topology for which multiplication and inversion are continuous. Let $M$ be a topological $K$-vector space with continuous $K$-linear left $G$-action (addition, negation, scalar multiplication and the action are continuous). Let $n\geq1$, let $H\subseteq G$ be an open subgroup with its induced topology [def-kun-subspace-topology], and choose $a_0,\ldots,a_n\in G$. Suppose $f:G^{n+1}\to M$ is continuous, is diagonally equivariant, $f(gg_0,\ldots,gg_n)=g f(g_0,\ldots,g_n)$, and is a homogeneous cocycle, meaning $\delta f=0$ for the differential $(\delta f)(g_0,\ldots,g_{n+1})=\sum_{i=0}^{n+1}(-1)^i f(g_0,\ldots,\widehat{g_i},\ldots,g_{n+1})$. If $f(h_0a_0,\ldots,h_na_n)=0$ for every $(h_0,\ldots,h_n)\in H^{n+1}$, then there is a continuous diagonally $H$-equivariant $t:H^n\to M$ with $f|_{H^{n+1}}=\delta t$, where $(\delta t)(h_0,\ldots,h_n)=\sum_{i=0}^{n}(-1)^i t(h_0,\ldots,\widehat{h_i},\ldots,h_n)$. The assertion concerns actual continuous cochains; no closure of the coboundaries or completeness of $M$ is imposed.

proof.text: Use integral formal chains: for a set $Y$, let $B_q(Y)$ be finite integer sums of ordered $(q+1)$-tuples from $Y$, with repeated entries allowed, using the specified tuple basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module], and let $B_{-1}(Y)=\mathbf Z$ generated by the empty tuple. The boundary $d$ is alternating deletion, with $d[y]=1$. Deleting positions $i<j$ in the two possible orders gives signs $(-1)^{i+j-1}$ and $(-1)^{i+j}$, so $d^2=0$, including augmentation. Extend $f$ additively to $F:B_n(G)\to M$. The stated cocycle identity says exactly $Fd=0$ on $B_{n+1}(G)$. Equivariance of $f$ and additivity of the action imply $F(gz)=gF(z)$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-ordered-join-partial-contraction] with $r=n+1$ and $X_i=Ha_i$ as separately labeled sets. Write $J$ for its augmented chains. Erasing color labels gives $e:J_q\to B_q(G)$; it commutes with $d$ because both boundaries delete the same ordered positions. Every degree-$n$ basis symbol has colors exactly $0,\ldots,n$ in that order, so the rectangle hypothesis gives $Fe=0$ on $J_n$. For each $h\in H$ choose the anchors $v_i(h)=ha_i$. The cited operator $S^h$ satisfies $dS^h+S^h d=1$ through degree $n-1$, including degree $-1$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion below local continuous-cocycle descent: explicit ordered-join chain calculation; not asserted in the blueprint itself.

proof.text: Construct augmented homomorphisms $P_q:B_q(H)\to J_q$ for $-1\leq q\leq n$. Set $P_{-1}=1$ and $P_0[h_0]=[(0,h_0a_0)]$, so $dP_0=P_{-1}d$. Suppose $P$ has been constructed through $q-1$, with $1\leq q\leq n$. For a basis tuple $x=[h_0,\ldots,h_q]$ put $z=P_{q-1}(dx)$ and define $P_q(x)=S^{h_0}_{q-1}(z)$, then extend additively. The induction hypothesis gives $dz=P_{q-2}d^2x=0$ (for $q=1$ use the already checked augmentation identity). Since $q-1\leq n-1$, the cited contraction gives $dP_q(x)=z$. Thus $dP_q=P_{q-1}d$ in every required degree. The anchor is selected separately on each input basis tuple; no claim of a single fixed-anchor chain contraction being $H$-equivariant is made.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion below local continuous-cocycle descent: explicit ordered-join chain calculation; not asserted in the blueprint itself.

proof.text: For $g\in H$, left translation maps $X_i$ to $X_i$ and takes $v_i(h)$ to $v_i(gh)$. Naturality in [lem-sfb-ordered-join-partial-contraction] therefore gives $gS^h(z)=S^{gh}(gz)$. Induction in the formula for $P_q$ now gives $P_q(gx)=gP_q(x)$, the base $q=0$ being $(gh_0)a_0=g(h_0a_0)$. Its finite-formula clause also gives, inductively, an expansion of each $P_q[h_0,\ldots,h_q]$ as a fixed finite integer sum of symbols whose vertices are $h_j a_i$. Indeed the boundary selects coordinate subtuples and the operator only inserts or replaces vertices by $h_0a_i$. All coefficients, color lists and coordinate choices are independent of the values of the $h_j$; coincident vertices are retained as uncancelled formal terms if necessary.

proof.text: Let $I_q:B_q(H)\to B_q(G)$ be coordinatewise inclusion and set $A_q=eP_q$. Both are augmented chain maps through degree $n$, both are $H$-equivariant, and $I_{-1}=A_{-1}=1$. For $b\in G$ define $C_b:B_q(G)\to B_{q+1}(G)$ by prefixing $b$, also $C_b(1)=[b]$ in degree $-1$. Direct deletion gives $d[b,y_0,\ldots,y_q]=[y_0,\ldots,y_q]-C_b(d[y_0,\ldots,y_q])$; in degree $-1$ it gives $d[b]=1$. Thus $dC_b+C_b d=1$ in all augmented degrees. Moreover $gC_bz=C_{gb}(gz)$.

proof.text:
Define $Q_{-1}=0$. Inductively, for $0\leq q\leq n$ and $x=[h_0,\ldots,h_q]$, put
$$Z_q(x)=I_qx-A_qx-Q_{q-1}(dx),\qquad Q_q(x)=C_{h_0}(Z_q(x)),$$
and extend $Q_q$ additively. For $q=0$ the augmentation of $Z_0$ is $1-1=0$. For $q\geq1$, the previous identity $dQ_{q-1}=I_{q-1}-A_{q-1}-Q_{q-2}d$ and the chain-map identities give
$$dZ_q=(I_{q-1}-A_{q-1})dx-(I_{q-1}-A_{q-1}-Q_{q-2}d)dx=0.$$
The prefix identity of the previous step therefore gives $dQ_q(x)=Z_q(x)$, hence
$$I_q-A_q=dQ_q+Q_{q-1}d.$$
This establishes the induction, including its base, without a resolution-comparison existence theorem.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion below local continuous-cocycle descent: explicit ordered-join chain calculation; not asserted in the blueprint itself.

proof.text: The recursion for $Q$ is equivariant: assuming it for $Q_{q-1}$, equivariance of $I,A,d$ gives $Z_q(gx)=gZ_q(x)$, and the identity for prefixing gives $Q_q(gx)=C_{gh_0}(gZ_q(x))=gQ_q(x)$. The base $Q_{-1}=0$ is equivariant. Likewise the finite-formula property for $A$, followed by subtraction, deletion and prefixing, proves by induction that every $Q_q[h_0,\ldots,h_q]$ has a fixed finite integer expansion in tuples whose coordinates are either some $h_j$ or some $h_ja_i$. This uses the explicit expansion proved in step 4; it introduces no choices or equality tests depending on the input.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion below local continuous-cocycle descent: explicit ordered-join chain calculation; not asserted in the blueprint itself.

proof.text: Define $t(h_0,\ldots,h_{n-1})=F(Q_{n-1}[h_0,\ldots,h_{n-1}])$. This is defined because $n\geq1$. The preceding expansion writes $t$ as a fixed finite sum of integer multiples of values $f(b_0(h),\ldots,b_n(h))$, where each $b_k(h)$ is a coordinate inclusion $h_j\in G$ or its right translate $h_ja_i$. The inclusion $H\to G$ is continuous by [def-kun-subspace-topology]; finite product projections are continuous by definition of the product topology, and right translation is continuous by the given multiplication. Hence every substituted tuple map is continuous, and so is its composite with $f$. Finite sums, negation and repeated addition are continuous by the hypotheses on $M$. Therefore $t$ is continuous. No topology on the formal chain groups is needed.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion below local continuous-cocycle descent: explicit ordered-join chain calculation; not asserted in the blueprint itself.

proof.text:
For $g\in H$, equivariance of $Q_{n-1}$ and of $F$ gives $t(gh_0,\ldots,gh_{n-1})=g\,t(h_0,\ldots,h_{n-1})$. In degree $n$ the homotopy identity gives
$$FI_n-FA_n=FdQ_n+FQ_{n-1}d.$$
Here $FA_n=FeP_n=0$ by the ordered rectangle hypothesis (step 2), and $FdQ_n=0$ by the homogeneous cocycle identity (step 1). Consequently $f(h_0,\ldots,h_n)=FQ_{n-1}d[h_0,\ldots,h_n]=\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^i t(h_0,\ldots,\widehat{h_i},\ldots,h_n)$, as required. This is an equality of actual cochains; the construction uses only finite integer sums, so it applies in every characteristic and imposes no completeness or closure hypothesis.
